monthly_review.summary: This month shows a sharp but narrow uptick in intensity and efficiency, driven by a single long run, while volume and frequency remain drastically lower than last month.
monthly_review.highlight: Despite only one run this month, the runner achieved their fastest pace of the period (531 sec/km) at an elevated average HR (147 bpm), indicating a shift toward higher-intensity work — but with no supporting volume or recovery context.

goal_tracker.message: You need 36.0 more km across 9 additional sessions to match last month’s volume — averaging 4.0 km per session over the remaining 29 days.

insights.title: Efficiency dip correlates with higher HR and reduced Z1/Z2 time
insights.body: Aerobic efficiency dropped from 13.42 to 12.81 m/sec per bpm this month, coinciding with a 22-point drop in Z1+Z2 time (79% → 46%) and +11 bpm average HR — suggesting less time spent in truly restorative zones is compromising metabolic economy.

insights.title: Zone 3–5 dominance (55% of time) replaces foundational aerobic base
insights.body: This month’s HR zone distribution shows 26% Z3, 22% Z4, and 7% Z5 — totaling 55% above Z2 — versus last month’s 22% (19% Z3 + 3% Z4 + 0% Z5), indicating a sudden departure from base-building toward threshold/VO2 work without prior volume support.

insights.title: Cadence increased but vertical oscillation rose with intensity
insights.body: Cadence improved from 146 to 154 spm, yet vertical oscillation increased from 7.5–7.8 cm (last month’s runs) to 7.9 cm (June 1), and ground contact time remained stable (~310 ms) — suggesting form efficiency may be straining under higher HR demands.

insights.title: Single high-TE run masks low overall training load
insights.body: The June 1 run delivered 3.5 aerobic TE — the highest of the month — but with only 1 run vs 10 last month, total monthly aerobic TE is ~3.5 vs ~27.0 (10 × avg 2.7), revealing a >85% reduction in cumulative stimulus despite the strong single-session output.

recommendations.action: Do a 5.0 km Zone 2 run (HR ≤135 bpm) on Tuesday, focusing on maintaining cadence ≥148 spm and vertical oscillation ≤7.6 cm.
recommendations.reason: Last month’s Z1+Z2 time was 79% and avg HR was 136 bpm; this brings back foundational stimulus while stabilizing form metrics observed in May’s lower-HR runs.

recommendations.action: Add a second easy run this week: 4.0 km at Zone 1–2 (HR 120–135 bpm), keeping stride length ≥71 cm and ground contact time ≤315 ms.
recommendations.reason: Recent runs show stride length drops below 71 cm when HR rises above 140 bpm (e.g., May 30: 81.96 cm but HR 142 bpm and VOsc 8.3 cm — outlier due to short distance); shorter, lower-HR efforts reinforce efficient mechanics.

recommendations.action: After your next two Zone 2 runs, do a 3.0 km progressive run: start at 550 sec/km (9:05 min/km), increase pace by 5 sec/km every km to finish at 535 sec/km (8:55 min/km), holding HR ≤145 bpm.
recommendations.reason: Your best recent pace is 531 sec/km (June 1) at 147 bpm — this builds race-pace familiarity at marginally lower HR to improve pace resilience without overstressing recovery.

weekly_focus.theme: Rebuild Aerobic Foundation with Form Awareness
weekly_focus.description: Prioritize consistent Zone 1–2 effort to restore Z1+Z2 time (>75%), lower average HR, and re-anchor running economy — using cadence, vertical oscillation, and ground contact time as real-time biofeedback.
suggested_sessions: Recovery-effort run with form focus (4 km)
